items.title: Residents fight opening of new cannabis shop in historic part of Mississauga
items.summary: Residents who strongly oppose the opening of a new cannabis shop in the historic Meadowvale Village area of Mississauga learned this week the city will seek a judicial review of the province’s decision to allow the business to operate. Mississauga city council voted following a closed session on Wednesday to have municipal legal staff continue to look at a decision of the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario to grant a retail licence to a cannabis store in the historic community in the city’s north end. , which is close to schools, parks and residential areas. “City staff will continue to gather information through the litigation process to assess the merits of the case and determine next steps,” Mississauga Ward 11 Coun. Brad Butt said this week in a letter to residents. “City staff will pursue discussions with the AGCO as well, if eligibility requirements were not met or there were errors in the decision-making process. “It is important to note that a judicial review is not a new legal hearing on whether this store should be approved or refused; success on judicial review would not necessarily result in refusal of the store,” Butt continued. “Rather, the court examines if the AGCO’s decision-making process was appropriate and reasonable under the applicable rules. ” Numerous area residents have signed a petition opposing the new shop, citing among other complaints that it will compromise the historic character of the neighbourhood. Some, including members of advocacy group Protect Old Meadowvale Village, demonstrated outside city hall this week as council considered its next step. The backlash comes from residents who believe the location of the store is too close to schools and homes in the heritage district, and that it will potentially expose young children to drug use. Furthermore, they allege the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario didn’t properly consult with them prior to approving the licence to operate.

items.title: House of the week: Indoor pool and 17 skylights features of this Mississauga home
items.summary: This place: This Lakeview home boasts 17 skylights, an indoor pool and four gas fireplaces. Features: This home offers over 4,200 square feet of total living space. Features include high ceilings, large windows, 17 remotely operated skylights, hardwood flooring, heated tile floors, custom millwork and four gas fireplaces. The custom kitchen showcases cabinetry, Miele appliances, granite countertops and a centre island with built-in refrigerators, a food warmer and a breakfast bar. A separate family room and upper-level library and office overlook the kitchen. A main-floor den/office could also be a guest bedroom. The primary bedroom has a cathedral ceiling, skylights, a gas fireplace, motorized shutters, a walk-in closet and an ensuite bathroom with a skylight and French doors. A second primary bedroom features a fireplace and an ensuite bathroom. There is another bedroom and a three-piece bathroom in the finished basement. The home has a 16-foot by 32-foot indoor pool, bar, sauna, hot tub and spa room with surround sound. The glass-enclosed pool area features a skylit ceiling, a dehumidification system, temperature-controlled heating and solar-assisted heating. Outside features include mature landscaping, a covered entertaining area, a built-in barbecue, and a private ravine setting backing onto the Etobicoke Creek. There are no rear neighbours.

items.title: Mississauga Truck Rollover on Hwy 401-410 Ramp: Your Injury Rights
items.summary: A transport truck rollover closed the ramp from westbound Highway 401 to northbound Highway 410 in Mississauga on Friday, November 27, 2026. Ontario Provincial Police warned drivers that the ramp would stay closed for most of the day. m. and was still there hours later. m. In a video posted online, Kerry Schmidt of the OPP described the truck's path. He said it travelled through the weeds, slid up an embankment, and then slid forward. He also said the truck's trailer buckled during the incident. Police reported minor injuries. However, they did not say who was hurt or whether anyone was taken to hospital. The OPP said the driver has been charged with careless driving under Ontario's traffic laws. A charge is not a finding of fault. The allegation has not been tested in court. The cleanup took longer than first expected.

items.title: Massive 176,000 sq. ft mega market now open in Mississauga
items.summary: After much anticipation, one of the biggest supermarkets to ever be built in Ontario has officially opened its doors in Mississauga. Food World Plus, located at 50 Matheson Blvd E. in the area of Eglinton and Hurontario, is a food enthusiast’s dream. This massive 176,000 sq. ft international mega market offers an impressive selection of multicultural and international foods all under one roof. A Hyundai Elantra, a 65-inch Roku TV, a weekend getaway to Elora Mill and two tickets to a Toronto Raptors game are among the exciting prizes up for grabs at Food World Plus! Shoppers can enter the grand prize draw for a chance to win by completing the entry form here. The store celebrated its grand opening on Friday, Oct. 30. It’s open every day: weekdays from 7 am to 10 pm, Saturdays from 8 am to 9 pm, and Sundays from 8 am to 8 pm. A destination for international foods and specialty ingredients Food World Plus is an international food and shopping destination in Mississauga. Spanning an expansive retail space, the mega market brings together an extensive selection of multicultural products, with dedicated aisles featuring international foods and specialty ingredients from East Asia and South Asia, Europe, the Mediterranean, Caribbean, and the Middle East. The experience extends across several departments, including fresh produce, a butcher section featuring Certified Angus beef and halal meats, seafood, bakery featuring specialty cakes and desserts, prepared foods, sushi, pizza, fresh churned gelato, deli and specialty cheeses, and wholesale offerings.

items.title: New Mississauga mayor tells U.S.-based firm appealing 1-year data centre ban to ‘bring it on’
items.summary: Get today's top news across Ontario for Nov. 27, 2026, inclu… According to Ontario Provincial Police, the westbound Highwa… The company with huge GTA footprint counters its proposal was well into the planning process before freeze. The city has launched a public engagement review as it continues studying impacts and benefits of data centres in Mississauga. Months after Mississauga’s one-year temporary freeze on large-scale data centre developments, two real estate firms are appealing the freeze at the Ontario Land Tribunal. -based industrial real estate firm Prologis and Toronto-based Montcrest Asset Management have both filed appeals against the interim control bylaw which came into effect on Sept. 16. The bylaw prohibits new or expansion of existing data centres with peak power demand of 10 megawatts or more as staff review planning and zoning rules. Prologis, which submitted a development application for a proposed data centre near Tenth Line West in Meadowvale Business Park, filed the appeal on Nov. 4. Speaking to reporters following council’s inaugural meeting on Nov. 16, Mayor Alvin Tedjo said the city is prepared to defend its bylaw at the tribunal.

items.title: New Shoppers Drug Mart opens in Mississauga
items.summary: A new Shoppers Drug Mart has just opened its doors in central Mississauga. The store opened Friday morning and it is the 34th Shoppers Drug Mart location in the city. It’s located at 175 Burnhamthorpe Road West, east of Duke of York Boulevard, in the heart of the city near Square One. The new store offers a range of health, beauty, and postal services, a news release from Shoppers said. “At the centre of the new location is a dedicated Pharmacy Care Clinic, designed to help patients access healthcare services closer to home,” the release said. ” The beauty department features a selection of international and specialty skincare brands. And as mentioned, the store also has a Canada Post office.

items.title: Mississauga Opens Public Feedback Period as Year-Long Data Centre Pause Continues
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents can now weigh in on how the city plans to manage future data centre applications as a review of the sector continues. The city says people can visit its website, watch information videos, submit questions or comments, and sign up for upcoming town halls to take part. The review follows a decision by city council in September 2026 to impose a one-year temporary pause on large-scale data centre developments while staff study the issue. The city noted that municipalities cannot automatically block this kind of development, but they can set rules governing how it moves forward. Officials say the study will look at local impacts, benefits and infrastructure needs tied to data centres, and will incorporate feedback from residents, partner agencies and other levels of government.

items.title: City honours Constable Dwayne Piukkala through bridge naming
items.summary: Members of the media are invited to attend a bridge naming ceremony recognizing the service and legacy of Peel Regional Police Constable Dwayne Piukkala. Entertainment and activities | November 27, 2026 The City of Mississauga is proud to honour the late Constable Piukkala by naming a bridge in his memory. His dedication to public service and commitment to the community continue to be remembered and celebrated. To mark this meaningful tribute, the ceremony will bring together Members of Mississauga Council, Peel Regional Police colleagues and representatives, City staff, community representatives and members of the Piukkala family. m. Ceremony Lake Wabukayne Pedestrian Bridge Crossing Winston Churchill Oka Road and Edenwood Drive (parking is available on street) [Map] Constable Dwayne Piukkala was a 24-year-old Peel Regional Police officer who was killed in the line of duty on August 26, 1984, after three years of service. He is being recognized for his service, dedication and lasting contributions to the community. The Lake Wabukayne Pedestrian Bridge, which crosses Winston Churchill Boulevard along Lake Wabukayne Trail in Ward 9, will now be named the Constable Dwayne Piukkala Bridge. This permanent reminder of his legacy gives future generations an opportunity to learn about and reflect on his commitment to public service. ca 905-615-3200, ext.

items.title: Poulet Rouge Preparing to Open New Restaurant on Courtneypark Drive in Mississauga
items.summary: Poulet Rouge is preparing to open a new restaurant at 98 Courtneypark Drive East, Unit C1, Mississauga, ON L5T 2Y3, according to the City of Mississauga’s 2026 building permit report. The filing lists interior alterations for the restaurant, while the brand’s official locations website identifies the Courtneypark location as “Opening soon”. According to Poulet Rouge’s website, the restaurant specializes in customizable meals built around grilled chicken, fresh ingredients and a choice of bases, sauces and toppings. Customers can build their own bowls, selecting ingredients to suit their preferences, with the menu offering options for different tastes and dietary needs. The restaurant’s menu features its Rouge Bowl, Rouge Mini and Rouge Poutine. The Rouge Bowl comes with two bases, one sauce and seven toppings, while the Rouge Mini includes one base, one sauce and three toppings. Customers can also order poutine with toppings and sauce, making the menu suitable for diners seeking either a lighter meal or a more indulgent option. Poulet Rouge offers several signature chicken flavours, including BBQ Sweet, Hercules Lemon, Shisha Garlic and Volcano Spicy. The official menu lists bases such as brown rice, bulgur wheat, quinoa, lettuce and kale, alongside sauces including Sweet Zaatar, Honey Dijon, Cilantro Lime, Caesar Ranch, Spicy Mayo and Smoky Chipotle. The brand’s website also highlights its fresh vegetables and customizable combinations, allowing customers to select ingredients and create bowls around their preferred flavours. The restaurant offers takeout and delivery at its locations, according to the company’s website. With its build-your-own format, the new Courtneypark restaurant will give Mississauga diners another option for customizable grilled chicken meals, bowls and poutine. Love our content? items.title: Anti-Black Racism Was a Factor in Son's Fatal Shooting by Police, Mississauga Mother Tells Inquest
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Ann-Marie White, the mother of Jamal Francique, testified at a coroner's inquest that she believes anti-Black racism played a role in her son's fatal shooting by Peel police nearly seven years ago. White said officers who testified could recall their training on use of force and firearms but not on anti-Black racism, leaving her to question whether there was a genuine effort to address bias. She said she remains troubled that about 25 minutes passed before her son got medical help after he was shot. White, the final witness at the inquest, said police resorted to an elaborate and botched plan to arrest Francique on Jan. 7, 2020, based on unconfirmed allegations. Police secretly surveilled Francique for days after a Crime Stoppers tip alleged he had drugs and a gun, but found nothing and arrested him instead for an alleged bail breach.
